content.storyline: Buffalo improved to 8-1, its best start in 35 years and its first 8-1 start since 1991. Josh Allen’s 325 regular-season touchdowns broke the record for the most by a player through his first 10 seasons; the 2-8 Jets suffered their fifth straight loss and had gone nine consecutive quarters without a touchdown.

basis.reasoning: The recap states Buffalo was 8-1 for the first time since 1991 and describes it as the franchise’s best start in 35 years; it also reports Allen’s 325-touchdown milestone. The recap says the Jets fell to 2-8, lost their fifth straight game, and had gone nine quarters without a touchdown.

excerpts: Allen ran for two scores and threw a TD pass to [DJ Moore](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3915416/dj-moore) , and the Bills pulled away from the [New York Jets](http://www.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/nyj/new-york-jets) for a 31-12 victory Sunday that has them at 8-1 for the first time since 1991, when they ... James Cook ran for 157 yards, including a 74-yard TD scamper in the fourth quarter that helped seal the win. It came with the Bills' league-leading offense hardly looking like a juggernaut through two quarters, when Buffalo led 10-6 before sending the Jets (2-8) to their fifth straight loss. “Honestly, offensively, we didn't play too well,” Allen said. “I know you can look at the stats sheet and (see) 31 points. I didn't feel like the first half we executed the way we wanted to." It wasn’t a huge statistical game for Allen, who went 11 of 21 for 196 yards with the TD and an interception — just the Jets’ second this season — and ran for 5 yards, including the two scoring runs. But Allen did make some more history. His 325 regular-season TDs (233 passing, 90 rushing and two receiving) broke a tie with Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning for the most by a player through their first 10 seasons — even though Allen is still in his ninth year.

But with what appeared to be at least half the crowd at MetLife Stadium decked out in blue, white and red Bills gear, the Jets managed just four field goals by [Jason Sanders](http://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3124679/jason-sanders) . New York has gone nine straight quarters without a touchdown.

recap.paragraph: James Cook races 74 yards for a Bills touchdown! Josh Allen also ran for 2 scores. His second put Buffalo ahead 17-9. Then Allen zipped a 45-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore. The Bills beat the Jets 31-12 and climbed to 8-1. Allen also broke the record for touchdowns by a player in his first 10 seasons.
